edges.description: In the organotypic thymoma arm, the neoplastic epithelium fails to enforce normal negative selection, generating autoreactive T cells.

Expansion of the transformed thymic epithelium within the prevascular compartment produces the anterior mediastinal mass that is the unifying clinical presentation across all three thymic neoplasm families.
Autoreactive T-cell escape supports pathogenic neuromuscular autoimmunity, the most common thymoma paraneoplastic syndrome.
Immune dysregulation from tolerance failure can suppress erythroid precursors.
Tolerance failure also underlies the thymoma-associated combined immunodeficiency of Good syndrome.

nodes.description: The unifying clinical presentation of thymic neoplasia: a prevascular (anterior) mediastinal mass, often found incidentally or when large enough to cause local compressive symptoms.

evidence.reference_title: Epidemiology of thymomas and thymic carcinomas in the United States and Germany, 1999-2019.
evidence.snippet: Among patients aged ≥20 years, TETs accounted for the most prevalent anterior mediastinal tumors (US/GER: 63%/64%), followed by lymphomas (14%/8%).

nodes.description: Thymoma-associated combined immunodeficiency (hypogammaglobulinemia with B-cell deficiency), the third classic paraneoplastic syndrome of thymoma alongside myasthenia gravis and pure red cell aplasia, predisposing to recurrent infections.

evidence.reference_title: Management of Autoimmune Conditions Associated With Thymic Epithelial Tumors.
evidence.snippet: Myasthenia gravis is the most common, followed by less frequent but notable conditions including pure red cell aplasia, Good's syndrome, and various neurologic, dermatologic, and systemic autoimmune disorders.

nodes.description: The thymoma-defining mechanism: a cortex-dominant, medulla-poor tumor microenvironment with loss of the autoimmune regulator (AIRE) generates autoreactive effector T cells and underproduces regulatory T cells, allowing self-reactive T-cell escape and paraneoplastic autoimmunity. The full causal chain (AIRE loss, residual medullary niches, neuromuscular autoantigen presentation) is curated in the Thymoma entry.

evidence.snippet: Recently, we also found that expression of the autoimmune regulator (AIRE) gene is absent from approximately 95% of thymomas.

nodes.description: The shared origin of the thymic epithelial and neuroendocrine tumor families: clonal proliferation of transformed thymic epithelial cells in the anterior mediastinum. The downstream biology then diverges by family - the organotypic thymoma arm perturbs thymic tolerance, while the carcinoma and neuroendocrine arms follow overtly malignant, higher-burden oncogenic programs detailed in the dedicated subtype entries.
